comments.value:
I downgraded my computer components and the issue resolved itself, however, I think I'm at a loss of 500 USD of computer parts for VRChat, time to exchange it for a new GPU ^^.
The issue I believe was GPU scheduling of a Turing GPU in parallel with the new 12th Gen Alder Lake CPU scheduling, something went horribly wrong and caused poor performance, less a bug VRChat could fix and more a driver and Unity version incompatibility that would be pointless for the devs to fix. (a unity version upgrade would probably resolve the issue, though
It just appears that this was a horrible incompatibility in computer components with VRChat, not much unfortunately that could've been done.

details:
GPU: 1660 Super (90th percentile)
CPU: i5-12600k (99th percentile)
Motherboard: MSI Pro-z690 DDR4
RAM: Dual channel, 16 GB 2700 MHz
TL;DR: Following the installation of a new CPU over this weekend, I and a couple of other users such as Banannete#2022 and Furriest#5231 with similar computer components had reported ambient VRChat gpu usage around 100% in home worlds and low fps in publics (more players on screen, worse fps, going down as low as 12-19 fps), drastically lower compared to prior to the upgrade and prior to last week (on Saturday) 
Contrasting the 100% usage of the gpu, the temps never really rise, meaning the GPU is not being utilized. Other applications do not suffer this issue and run fine. Issue appears to be consistent with Intel devices, The other user was also using a GTX 16xx series card as well, using a 1650 super. Issue persists even after reinstalling and uninstalling graphics drivers, doing benchmarks to see baseline performance (which were great) and even after reinstalling windows wiped clean twice, once on windows 11, and now on windows 10. Checked for every possible issue and it appears that there is an issue in the DirectX runtime for Turing cards. VRChat is the only game with this issue, and this issue popped up last Saturday for me and another user.
I've reinstalled windows twice on two different versions and tried WDDM (windows default) and Nvidia graphics drivers, exact same issue. It appears to be related to some DirectX bug specific to VRChat from my findings, as no issue on my computer's side could be found, thermals were all fine, all games (Minecraft with really expensive shaders) were butter smooth! For now, I'm unable to play VRChat with the low FPS, and in VR the frame rates get much worse.
Funny thing is the FPS issues go away and the frame rates are always at their capped values when I have "-force-d3d12" active, but you can't play in VR in d3d12 mode (VRChat, please fix.), which would be a nice feature to have, which I why I made it a feature request. FPS issues also ceased for Banannete by turning the "-force-d3d12" on in steam launch options, but this still gatekeeps from VR because VRChat has yet to implement that into their application for VR.
title: [DirectX 11 Bug | Unity 2020.1.1- 2020.1.2] Hideously low (14-45) FPS after upgrading PC components, but FPS soars past 100-150 in "-force-d3d12" mode (but with no VR capability)
